indicator_definition: This indicator measures the number of fatal accidents at work per 100,000 persons employed. A fatal accident at work is defined as an accident that leads to the death of the victim within one year of the accident. Data are collected through the European Statistics on Accidents at Work (ESAW).
rationale: Ensuring safe and healthy working conditions is a fundamental dimension of decent work. Fatal accidents at work represent a preventable loss of life with severe consequences for workers, families and society. Progress means a sustained reduction in the rate of fatal accidents at work.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat through the European Statistics on Accidents at Work (ESAW) methodology. The indicator covers all accidents at work that result in the death of the victim within one year. Data are published annually.
